newsitem.title: USA: Enron adds coal assets to energy portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Enron adds coal assets to energy portfolio.

text.p: Enron Corp diversified its energy holdings on Thursday with a $149 million acquisition of domestic lignite reserves from rival NGC Corp, the company said.

Analysts said the addition of lignite reserves to Enron's energy portfolio will allow the Houston-based company to arbitrage the soft coal used to fuel electric power plants for electrons that could then be sold into domestic markets opened to competition.
"I can only assume this is another form of Btu (British thermal unit) and Btu delivery capability," Credit Suisse-First Boston analyst Steven Parla said.

For its part, Enron declined to discuss its plans for the lignite reserves and other assets in Michigan, Colorado, New Mexico and Texas. "We are still evaluating these assets," a spokeswoman said. "At this point in time, I can't elaborate."

The deal comes on the heels of PacifiCorp's purchase of Britain's Energy Group Plc and its Peabody coal subsidiary, the world's largest private coal producer with operations in the United States and Australia.

As the U.S. electric industry is deregulated, arbitraging fuel sources like natural gas and coal for electrons is one of several strategies being pursued by companies jockeying to sell electricity in the wholesale and retail markets.

Enron has set its sights on garnering a 10 percent share and $20 billion in gross revenues by 2001 in the domestic retail natural gas and electric market. The company on July 1 closed its $3 billion strategic merger with Portland General Corp, boosting its assets to about $19 billion.
